summary: Manchester United beat Chelsea 2-1 at Old Trafford in the Premier League, thanks to a Scott McTominay brace (19' and 70') either side of a Cole Palmer equaliser on 45'. The win moved United within three points of Manchester City, who lost to Aston Villa, and made McTominay the club's top scorer with six goals. Erik ten Hag dismissed talk of a crisis after a week of reports of disunity, while the article also covers a minute-by-minute log, lineups, injuries and viewing options.
one_line: Scott McTominay's two goals gave Manchester United a 2-1 Premier League win over Chelsea at Old Trafford, easing pressure on Erik ten Hag.
key_facts: Manchester United beat Chelsea 2-1 at Old Trafford, with McTominay scoring on 19' and 70' and Cole Palmer equalising for Chelsea on 45'.
The win put United within three points of Manchester City, who were defeated by Aston Villa, and keeps them in reach of the top four.
Scott McTominay became United's top scorer this season with six goals, one ahead of Bruno Fernandes and Rasmus Hojlund.
Bruno Fernandes had a ninth-minute penalty saved by Robert Sanchez after Antony was fouled by Enzo Fernandez; the penalty was awarded after VAR advised referee Chris Kavanagh to review.
Rasmus Hojlund was substituted after another Premier League game without a goal, despite making 11 appearances.
Cole Palmer, 21, who joined Chelsea from Manchester City in August, scored his fifth Premier League goal of the season and his first from open play.
McTominay had seven shots, his most ever in a league game.
United have now won their past 19 Premier League games at Old Trafford when scoring first, including all 16 under Erik ten Hag.
Ten Hag said of crisis talk: "Crisis? Not for us. We keep calm. We know where we have to build."
Marcus Rashford started on the bench, a decision described as eyebrow-raising, while Mauricio Pochettino started Cole Palmer.
Reece James and Marc Cucurella returned for Chelsea after suspension; Reece James came on at half-time for Cucurella and Sergio Reguilon replaced Victor Lindelof for United.
Conor Gallagher was banned after two yellow cards against Brighton; Casemiro and Lisandro Martinez remained out for United.
Raheem Sterling has failed to score in any of his 24 matches against Man United, and Chelsea have been without a league win at Old Trafford since 2013.
Armando Broja hit the post in the 90th minute, nearly equalising for Chelsea.
